contentBlocks.body: A repository hides how records are stored behind a small interface: add, get, update, remove, list. Callers do not know whether data lives in a Map, a database or an API, which makes the storage easy to swap and easy to fake in tests.

Returning copies protects the repository's invariants. If get returned the stored object, a caller could change item.id and corrupt the Map without going through any method. Ids should also never be reused: a counter that only goes up guarantees that a removed record's id cannot accidentally point at a new one.

The exercise harness can only compare plain data, so the exercise drives the class through a list of commands and returns what each call produced. This is also a handy way to write readable tests for stateful classes.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why does get return `{ ...item }` instead of `item`?

choices: because Map values cannot be returned directly
so callers cannot mutate the stored record behind the repository's back
to convert the id to a string
payload.answer: so callers cannot mutate the stored record behind the repository's back
payload.explanation: A shallow copy means changes to the returned object do not affect what the repository stores.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Items 1 and 2 exist. Item 2 is removed, then a new item is added. With a #nextId counter, what id does it get?

payload.explanation: The counter only moves forward, so ids are never reused.

payload.text: Calling map.____(id) removes the entry and returns true if it existed.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Implement InMemoryRepo with private storage and ids starting at 1. runRepo feeds it commands and returns each result.
